title: Sugar

description.main: Sugar (self-published, New Haven, 2016) is the third and final book of Aaron McElroy's Sugar series: wire-bound black and white nudes laser-printed by the artist. 55 pages, 48 illustrations, 8 x 11 inches, edition of 120.
description.extended:
Sugar closes Aaron McElroy's Sugar series, three wire-bound books of black and white nudes that he published himself across 2015 and 2016.

Published in 2016 from New Haven, it runs to 55 pages with 48 black and white illustrations at 8 x 11 inches, in an edition of 120. As in the two earlier volumes, old and recent nudes sit side by side, reduced to line and shape by the flat blacks and broken tones of McElroy's laser printing. The white cover carries only the title in blue script. On his own site he offered the book alone or with a signed print from an edition of 10.

McElroy is a New York photographer and a founder of S_U_N, the cooperative behind Sweet (2015), the first book of the series, and The Devil May Care (2014), his largest book. Candy (2015) is the second volume. Dashwood Books sold the three together as a signed set of 50 copies, and the library holds all three.
description.artist_bio: Aaron McElroy (b. 1978, Daytona) is a New York photographer and a founding member of S_U_N, the photographers' cooperative. Studied at the New England School of Photography. Books include The Devil May Care (S_U_N, 2014), Sweet (S_U_N, 2015), Reds (S_U_N) and Briney Breezes (with Charles Johnstone, 2015).

notes: Sugar Series, volume 3 of 3. Signed by McElroy. Edition of 120 per photo-eye, the artist's own site (archived July 2017) and josefchladek.com; no source disagrees. Specs (55 pp., 48 b/w ills., 8x11 in, New Haven, 2016) from photo-eye, which gives no paper stock for this volume; josefchladek.com gives 74 pages and 21 x 28 cm approx. Dashwood sold the three volumes as a set limited to 50, each signed; that figure is the set, not this volume. The artist also offered the book with a signed print in an edition of 10. Cover file is photo-eye's flat product image, 219x298, the only flat front cover found; the artist-site images are not archived.
